Class SimpleStat

Namespace
ShapeEngine.Stats
Assembly
ShapeEngine.dll

Represents a simple stat with a base value and modifiers that affect it. Use SimpleStat When:

  • Small-scale games: Mobile puzzle game with 3-5 stats
  • Prototypes: Quick iteration, don't need polish
  • Isolated systems: One-off calculations, temporary stats
  • Performance-critical: Thousands of stat instances updated per frame
  • No UI needs: Players don't need to see "why" values are what they are

For are more advanced systems, use StatSet.

Remarks

  • A base value and upper/lower bounds can be set.
  • Modifiers can be added, removed, and stacks of modifiers can be adjusted (reduced, increased).
  • Modifiers have an ID to identify them.
  • Modifiers can be permanent or timed. Timed modifiers that will run out are completely removed.
  • Adding stacks refreshes the modifier's remaining duration, if it is timed.
  • Removing stacks to 0 or below will remove the modifier.
  • Max stacks can be used to cap the stack number that can be reached. Timer will still be refreshed on timed modifiers.
  • There are flat, additive percentage, multiplicative percentage, override, min, and max modifiers.
  • Flat modifiers are summed up and added to the base value. Stacks apply.
  • Additive percentage modifiers are summed up and then multiplied with the current value. Stacks apply.
  • Each multiplicative modifier is multiplied with the current value separately for the amount of stacks it has.
  • If at least 1 override modifier is active the override value with the highest priority is used to set the current value directly. No flat or percentage modifiers are applied. Stacks are ignored.
  • The min and max modifiers with the highest priority are used to clamp the current value. Stacks are ignored.
  • The stats bounds are used (if set) to clamp the current value.
  • If priority is tied for 2 modifiers, the modifier with the higher ID wins.

Fields

BoundsModifierTieBehaviourId

Determines how tied priorities are resolved when multiple Min or Max modifiers compete. When true, the modifier with the higher ID takes precedence. When false, the stricter bound is applied (highest minimum or lowest maximum).

public static bool BoundsModifierTieBehaviourId

Field Value

bool

Examples

Min Modifier Tie Resolution:

  • Min modifier: 10 (priority 5)
  • Min modifier: 20 (priority 3)
  • When true: value of 10 is used (higher ID wins).
  • When false: value of 20 is used (stricter lower bound wins).

Max Modifier Tie Resolution:

  • Max modifier: 100 (priority 5)
  • Max modifier: 60 (priority 3)
  • When true: value of 100 is used (higher ID wins).
  • When false: value of 60 is used (stricter upper bound wins).

AddModifier(uint, float, StatModifierKind, float, int, int, int)

Adds a new modifier to the stat or sets the values of an existing one if the ID already exists for the specified kind. If existing modifier is found, it is updated with the new values.

public bool AddModifier(uint id, float value, StatModifierKind kind, float duration = -1, int stacks = 1, int maxStacks = 0, int priority = 0)

Parameters

id uint

The unique identifier for the modifier.

value float

The value of the modifier.

kind StatModifierKind

The kind of modifier.

duration float

The duration of the modifier. Use PermanentDuration for permanent modifiers. 0 counts as permanent too!

stacks int

The number of stacks to start with.

maxStacks int

The maximum number of stacks allowed for this modifier.

priority int

The priority of the modifier (used for override, min, and max kinds).

Returns

bool

True if the modifier was successfully added or updated; otherwise, false.
